Sources indicate that ⁠Nvidia has made clear⁠ it won’t backstop an AI data center until it’s nearly ready to run, and that’s landing just as neoclouds report construction delays and more expensive debt. The message to developers is that land, power, and a finished building matter more than a pitch deck.

In a recent development, ⁠Anita Verma-Lallian⁠ has been selling exactly that. Her firm, Arizona Land Consulting, assembles data center sites for developers, hyperscalers, AI labs, and neoclouds, giving her a view into who’s buying, what makes a site viable, and where projects are running into trouble. She also partners with investor ⁠Chamath Palihapitiya,⁠ who has been predicting an industry shakeout.

Shiba Inu (SHIB) gained 5.96% over the past 24 hours and traded at $0.0000038 on Monday, according to CoinMarketCap, as talk of a December "Santa rally" returned to the crypto market. Still, SHIB is down 8.86% over the past seven days, and the token has lost 18.5% in November so far, according to CryptoRank.

Last week, SHIB dropped to $0.00000337, its lowest level since 2021.

According to recent reports, the hopes for a Santa rally come after Goldman Sachs analysts said last week that most of the December gains on the stock market usually come after Dec. 15. SHIB's own December history, however, shows that the Santa rally came for the token once in five years.

Recent findings suggest that according to CryptoRank, SHIB lost 29.5% and 13.5% in December of 2021 and 2022, respectively. In December of 2023, the token gained 24.6%. In December of 2024 and 2025, SHIB lost 21% and 17.6%, respectively.

SHIB's median December return is -17.6%, and its average December return is -11.4%, according to CryptoRank data.

It has been revealed that the green December of 2023 came after SHIB gained 6.04% in October and 6.62% in November of that year, according to CryptoRank. In 2026, SHIB lost 18.6% in October, and November is also in the red so far.

The Goldman note, titled "GS Flow of Funds: Chopsgiving," came from Gail Hafif, Brian Garrett and Lee Coppersmith, who looked at S&P 500 data going back to 1928. According to the note, the index usually gains 1.1% from mid-November to early December and then gives back about two-thirds of that gain by mid-December, and around 80% of the full 2.4% gain comes after Dec. 14-15.

Since 1990, the S&P 500 has risen after Dec. 15 in 27 of 36 years, according to Goldman.

The Goldman team called these figures a historical map. In the years when the VIX volatility index was above 18 in the middle of November, the S&P 500 gained 1.34% on average, and the index ended the year higher in 59% of cases, according to the note. According to Goldman, the VIX was above that level in mid-November of this year as well.

Goldman also noted that retail investors have been buying massive tech and chip stocks. Large funds and systematic traders have been cutting their positions, according to the note.

According to recent reports, the Stock Trader's Almanac counts the last five trading days of December and the first two trading days of January as the Santa Claus rally. This season, the window will open on Dec. 24 and close on Jan. 5.

In a recent development, in the window that ended on Jan. 5, 2026, the S&P 500 declined 0.11%, according to the Almanac. "Santa was a no-show for the third year in a row," the Almanac wrote. Before that, the S&P 500 also ended the Santa Claus rally windows of 2023 and 2024 lower.

Stellar recorded $207.2 million in tokenized funds in the seven days to November 22, reaffirming continued institutional interest in the blockchain.

Industry observers note that the RWA Foundation shared data in a post using figures from Token Terminal showing that Stellar ranked among the top blockchains in tokenized fund growth in the seven days from November 15 to November 22, 2026. Stellar recorded $207.2 million: Franklin Templeton added $108.0 million and Spiko added $68.2 million.

According to recent reports, .@injective led tokenized fund growth this past week. @StellarOrg had a good week also. https://t.co/7Ip2oK6c1X.

This means Stellar continues to grow in tokenized assets, a major highlight of strong growth in Q3, 2026.

Sources indicate that real-world assets tokenized on Stellar amounted to $4.1 billion at the end of Q3 2026, up 36% from Q2 and up 548% from Q3 2025. Two assets drove the bulk of the quarter’s growth: Tradable’s latest tokenized private credit and continued inflows into the Spiko Amundi overnight swap fund.

In late August 2026, Stellar held more tokenized non-US government debt than any other blockchain, with about $490 million in sovereign instruments. These included Spiko’s euro Treasury bill fund, Mexican CETES and Brazilian Tesouro bonds through Etherfuse, South Korean Treasury bonds, and a Marshall Islands digital sovereign bond.

Stellar has widened access to tokenized funds in the United States, Europe and Asia. Franklin Templeton’s BENJI has been on Stellar since 2021. In August 2026, the SEC's Division of Investment Management issued a no-action letter confirming that the Franklin Templeton's registered mutual funds and ETFs may use BENJI for cash management. This expands the set of institutions permitted to hold it. Franklin Templeton made a similar move in Europe, registering 'grBenji' as a Luxembourg UCITS share class for third-party distribution, now live on 21X.

Sources indicate that in Asia, Marketnode announced in August that it will offer funds from BNY Investments on Stellar, with Marketnode acting as the tokenization and distribution platform. Together, these developments expand access to tokenized funds on Stellar for institutions in the United States, Europe and Asia.

State Street Investment Management and Galaxy brought their Onchain Liquidity Sweep Fund to Stellar in September 2026.

The past weeks have seen the broad crypto ETF market face consistent withdrawals from investors, causing Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Solana, and others to record steady outflows since October.

While the negative trend has continued, Solana has just taken over the leadership in the broad ETF market after recording its first inflow in a while.

Latest data from SosoValue shows that while Bitcoin, Ethereum, and XRP ETFs have continued to struggle with consistent weekly outflows, Solana has just beaten the trend after it finally ended a six-week streak of consecutive weekly outflows.

Notably, the data shows that Solana spot ETFs have recorded a net inflow of $4.38 million over the week.

Although the net amount of capital received by the ETFs appears decent, it is significant considering the growing crypto market weakness.

While this marks an end to the Solana ETFs' six-week outflow streak, this is the first positive weekly performance they have recorded since October 9.

Further data shows that Bitcoin spot ETFs suffered the largest withdrawals as investors pulled out about $1.79 billion during the same period.

The negative trend also extended to the Ethereum ETF market as the funds posted a total of $314.17 million in net outflows following the consistent selling pressure.

In addition to this, the XRP spot ETFs were not spared, as the funds recorded $11.11 million in weekly outflows, leaving Solana as the only one among the four major crypto ETFs to finish the week on a positive note.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon Musk called YouTuber Marques Brownlee “a chicken” early Saturday, hours after Tesla opened invite-only Cybercab orders at $29,990 and Brownlee argued that his famous head-shaving bet isn’t lost.

Tesla has about seven weeks to get a Cybercab into a customer’s hands for under $30,000 before 2027, but the half-baked version of Cybercab that they opened orders for with delivery in December makes it look like it’s just to win this dumb bet.

Industry observers note that surely Tesla isn’t down enough to deliver a half-baked product just to “prove” a YouTuber wrong? Or is it?

Sources indicate that after Tesla’s “We, Robot” event in October 2024, Brownlee (MKBHD) noted there was no way Tesla would deliver a Cybercab to a customer for $30,000 or less before 2027. If it did, he’d shave his head on camera.

Musk has taken it personally ever since. When the first Cybercab came off the Giga Texas line in February, he replied “Gonna happen 😂” to a bald-MKBHD meme, which we covered at the time. In September, after Brownlee doubled down in a fresh video, Musk wrote: “I guess he really wants to shave his head 🤷‍♂️”.

Sources indicate that on Friday, Tesla started inviting “select customers” to buy a Cybercab for personal use. The order page lists $29,990, a mandatory $299 per month Autonomy Subscription, a $1,000 non-refundable deposit, and an estimated delivery of December 2026, only in Tesla’s Texas Robotaxi cities.

According to recent reports, as we reported Friday, the car only operates inside Tesla’s Robotaxi geofences. And Tesla’s Cybercab Autonomy Subscription Agreement says it “will not operate” without the $299 proposal, bans owners from putting it on the Robotaxi network or using it for ride-hailing, and lets Tesla shrink the operating area at any time.

So Tesla designed a robotaxi, then offered it to select private owners who aren’t allowed to use it as a taxi. Over five years, that’s $47,631 before insurance, registration, and charging. And you are limited to small geofenced areas. If you stop paying Tesla’s monthly fee, which it can change at all times, your cybercab becomes a paperweight.

Industry observers note that brownlee laid out his case Friday night. There are no deliveries yet, the car is invite-only rather than publicly available, and it can’t be used as a cab outside of the existing geofences. He called it “a paperweight if I take this thing home,” though he admits that last point isn’t technically part of the bet.

The memes are everywhere, so let’s go back over the bet: Cybercab publicly available for under $30k by the end of 2026My hair is safe for several reasons1: No deliveries yet. But they’re estimating starting in December so that’s neat2: Invite only, not actually publicly… https://t.co/NCD2aFbe2c.

Tesla fans fired back with clips from his September video, where he described a car that “will not ship to regular people like you and me for $30k before the end of 2026.” Whole Mars Catalog, an Elon Musk propagandist whose real name is Omar Qazi, told him to “be a man and honor your word.” Musk reposted it, then replied:.

Musk also reposted a Grok answer claiming the current offer “matches” the conditions of the bet.

But around the same time, Musk replied directly to Brownlee’s post about the order page, and it didn’t help Tesla’s case:.

According to recent reports, “It will be available nationwide, as we receive regulatory approval. But the monthly fee is too high. Should match the cost of Tesla FSD and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month.”.

Industry observers note that that’s Tesla’s CEO confirming, a day after launch, that the car can’t be sold outside the areas where it already operates and that its price is wrong. A price that Musk fully controls.

According to recent reports, yes, it looks like Tesla is rushing this out just to win a bet against a Youtuber. Absolutely insane behavior. We’ve seen this movie before. In June 2025, Tesla did a single “autonomous delivery” of a Model Y to meet a Musk deadline, then never did it again.

Industry observers note that tesla always pitched the Cybercab as a vehicle for its Robotaxi network. Now, seven weeks before the deadline, a personal-use version indicates up that’s invite-only, Texas-only, banned from doing the one thing it was designed for, and attached to a subscription Musk himself says is too expensive. If you set out to build a product whose main job was letting Musk claim he won a Twitter bet, it would look a lot like this.

This Cybercab offering is completely broken. The value proposition is awful. As others have put it, it’s a permanent variable rate lease starting at $300 a month with a ridiculous $30,000 down payment.

Besides, the bet was "under 30k." Starting price is under 30k, but a subscription is required, which takes it over 30k, just to use it for one day. They could have given the car away for free, and just charged a fee to use it. Doesn't change the total cost.

"Real bottom will not occur until October 2026," Brandt stated in an interview in February.

Volkswagen revealed how much its latest ID. Cross will cost, with prices starting at around $35,000 in the UK. But if you’re hoping to get the cheaper version, you’ll have to wait a bit longer.

Industry observers note that after opening orders for the ID. Cross in Europe in July, Volkswagen is preparing to launch the entry-level electric SUV in the UK.

The ID. Cross is the all-electric equivalent of the T-Cross, Volkswagen’s smallest and most affordable SUV in Europe and the UK.

Following the ID. Polo, the ID. Cross is the latest from Volkswagen’s electric urban family of compact cars.

It has been revealed that the electric SUV is 4,153 mm long, about the same length as the T-Cross, but its dedicated MEB+ platform offers more interior space. It seats five and offers a 475-liter boot, 20 liters more than the gas-powered T-Cross with the rear seats pushed all the way forward.

When the rear seats are folded, the electric ID. Cross offers up to 1,345 liters of overall luggage volume.

In a recent development, like in Europe, the Volkswagen ID. Cross will be available with two battery packs in the UK: a 37 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) pack and a 52 kWh nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) pack.

The ID. Cross with the larger 52 kWh battery offers up to 265 miles of WLTP range, while the 37 kWh version provides up to 194 miles of WLTP range.

With DC fast charging of up to 105 and 88 kW, Volkswagen said the vehicle’s battery can charge from 10% to 80% in as little as 23 minutes.

All versions are equipped with vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities, allowing it to be used as a mobile power bank for an e-bike, campsite, or other external electronic devices.

Inside, the ID. Cross adopts VW’s revamped interior digital cockpit design. Cross adopts VW’s revamped interior digital cockpit design. The setup includes a 10.25″ Digital Cockpit Pro instrument display and a 12.9″ infotainment screen. Based on driver feedback, Volkswagen brought back physical buttons for climate control and other vehicle functions.

Volkswagen will open orders for the ID. Cross Life and Style trims in the UK with the 52 kWh battery and 208 hp (211 PS) motor will go on sale on Thursday, November 19, starting at £30,260 ($40,000) and £33,675 ($44,500), respectively.

According to recent reports, the base ID. Cross Life and Style trims with the 37 kWh battery will go on sale in January 2027, with prices starting at £26,985 ($35,500) and £30,400 ($40,100).

Volkswagen remarked the 52 kWh version is eligible for the UK government’s £1,500 ($2,000) electric car grant. Eligibility for the 37 kWh versions is expected to be confirmed soon.

In Europe, Volkswagen opened orders for the entry-level ID. Cross Trend last month, starting at €27,995 ($31,000) in Germany, including VAT.

As the electric counterpart to its popular T-Cross, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer noted the ID. Cross is “modern, reliable, and above all, affordable.”.

Sadly, VW has no plans to bring the ID. Cross to the US. In early 2027, it will launch the latest ID. Tiguan, which will replace the outgoing ID.4 SUV.

The firm's recent purchase comes as the leading cryptocurrency has been struggling to rebound from the heavy sell-off that recently dragged it to a two-plus-year low.

The latest data from Strategy's SEC filing reveals that the firm has bought 457 Bitcoin at an average price of $64,898 per coin.

The new purchase brings Strategy’s Bitcoin holdings to around 851,305 BTC, which accounts for over 4% of the cryptocurrency's maximum supply of 21 million coins.

The firm has now spent around $64.23 billion to build its Bitcoin holdings at an average price of $75,446 per Bitcoin.

It is worth noting that Strategy has been buying BTC at gradually decreasing prices as the cryptocurrency market continues to bleed heavily.

Sources indicate that on Nov. 2, the firm announced that it had bought 811 BTC, worth around $65.5 million, at an average price of $80,846 per Bitcoin.

A week later, on Nov. 9, Strategy confirmed the purchase of 1,036 BTC worth $81.9 million at an average price of $79,012.

The firm’s Bitcoin purchase a week later, on Nov. 16, was relatively smaller at 485 BTC, worth $33.4 million, with an average price of $68,887.

The latest 457 BTC purchase continues this pattern. The latest Strategy purchase was made at an almost 20% lower price than the firm’s Nov. 2 acquisition.

Overall, the firm has made four weekly purchases, scooping up around 2,789 BTC worth $210.4 million.

However, these purchases have been much smaller than before. The latest $29.6 million purchase is almost 64% lower than the $81.9 million purchase announced just two weeks ago.

Although Saylor is doubling down on Bitcoin, Strategy’s massive holdings in the cryptocurrency are underwater as the market has been struggling to regain its footing.

Industry observers note that on Nov. 21, Bitcoin hit a low of around $55,130, its lowest level since September 2024, before rebounding above $61,000.

The firm’s recent purchases have helped reduce its overall average Bitcoin acquisition cost, but the drop has not been that significant.

For example, with the latest purchase, the average cost of the firm’s Bitcoin holdings dropped from $75,452 to around $75,446, a decline of just $6 per Bitcoin.

At the same time, the firm has also been putting a lot of resources into supporting its preferred securities.

In the latest reporting period, Strategy sold around 1.93 million common shares, raising net proceeds of $176.7 million.

#122612. Breaking: Tesla on Autopilot/FSD hit an overturned truck at 71 mph, killing 3

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1513 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Tesla on Autopilot/FSD hit an overturned truck at 71 mph, killing 3

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1513 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A Tesla Model 3 drove into an overturned box truck on I-75 near Naples, Florida, killing two of its passengers and a man who had stopped to help.
  • Police and local media covered the May 31 crash as a truck wreck in the dark, and none of it mentioned a driver-assist system.
  • Recent findings suggest that just before 4 a.m.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A Tesla Model 3 drove into an overturned box truck on I-75 near Naples, Florida, killing two of its passengers and a man who had stopped to help. Tesla’s own report to federal regulators states Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving” was engaged, at 71 mph.

Police and local media covered the May 31 crash as a truck wreck in the dark, and none of it mentioned a driver-assist system. It’s the latest case in our ongoing investigation into fatal crashes hidden in Tesla’s NHTSA data, and it lands as Tesla’s monthly crash count hits another record.

Recent findings suggest that just before 4 a.m. on Sunday, May 31, 2026, the 31-year-old driver of a 2014 Freightliner lost the road near the Pine Ridge Road exit in Collier County, steered back onto southbound I-75, and flipped it, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The overturned truck ended up blocking the center and outside lanes.

In a recent development, jonathan Garcia Arias, a 25-year-old Naples man and former Marine, was driving by in a BMW. He pulled over and got out to help the truck driver.

According to recent reports, then a southbound 2023 Tesla with five young men from Naples inside came up on the scene. FHP’s report says the front of the Tesla hit the underside of the overturned truck and Garcia Arias. Two of the Tesla’s passengers, aged 18 and 19, died at the scene, and Garcia Arias died later in the hospital. The 20-year-old driver and two more passengers were seriously hurt.

It has been revealed that A few days later, FHP used the crash as a warning about stopping near wrecks on the interstate. Senior Trooper Kenn Watson said the Tesla driver would have seen only the truck’s underside, with “no lights, no reflectors, nothing warning them.”.

It has been revealed that so that’s the official story. A dark obstacle, a driver who couldn’t see it in time. Nobody said a word about Autopilot.

According to recent reports, under NHTSA’s Standing General Order, automakers have to report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact and someone was killed or hurt. Tesla filed one for this crash.

It identifies the car as a 2023 Model 3 on a highway, flags a traffic incident on the roadway, and marks the automation “Engagement Status” as “Verified Engaged.” That means Tesla confirmed through its own telematics that Autopilot or FSD was on. It logs a pre-crash speed of 71 mph and a fatality, lists the Florida Highway Patrol as the investigating agency, and says it learned of the crash from police and the media.

Then it blacks out the crash narrative, the software version, and whether the road was within the system’s approved operating domain, all as “confidential business information.” That’s the same redaction Tesla applies to 99.9% of its reports.

The report also surfaced late. Tesla filed it as a 5-Day report, the urgent category for fatal crashes, but it didn’t land until Tesla’s September filings, more than three months after the crash. And Tesla lists law enforcement as one of the ways it found out about it.

According to recent reports, how we matched it: Tesla logged the incident time as 07:56 UTC, which converts to 3:56 a.m. in Florida, two minutes off the 3:54 a.m. in FHP’s report. The city, the highway, the 2023 model year, the month and the fatal outcome all line up, and it’s the only fatal Tesla driver-assist report in Naples that month. It’s the same crash.

A Tesla on driver-assist going highway speed into the underside of a big truck, in the dark, in Florida. If that sounds familiar, it should.

Industry observers note that in 2016, Joshua Brown was killed near Williston when his Model S on Autopilot drove under a tractor-trailer crossing the highway. In 2019, Jeremy Banner died in Delray Beach when his Model 3 on Autopilot went under a trailer at 68 mph and had its roof sheared off. In both crashes, neither the driver nor the system braked.

Trooper Watson’s point was that a human couldn’t see the truck. But a massive, unlit obstacle sitting across two lanes at night is exactly the kind of thing a driver-assist system is supposed to catch, and Tesla now sells FSD as nearly ready to drive with nobody watching. And an attentive driver could clearly see it, as the BMW driver did, and stop before the Tesla arrived.

We want to be fair about what the data doesn’t prove. “Engaged within 30 seconds” is the reporting trigger. Tesla’s 71 mph may be a telematics snapshot rather than the impact speed. And with the software version redacted, we can’t say whether this was Autopilot or FSD.

In a recent development, the NHTSA release that surfaced this crash, covering filings through October 15, also set a upcoming monthly high. Tesla reported 264 driver-assist crashes in September 2026, beating July’s 236, which was itself a record. That’s up from 135 in March.

In a recent development, september may still grow as late reports come in. This Naples crash indicates how late they can be.

According to recent reports, our merged dataset now holds 4,669 Tesla driver-assist crash reports since 2019, 69 of them flagged fatal. The same release added two other fatal reports, both “Verified Engaged” and both covered locally with no mention of driver-assist: a Model Y that hit a tree and burned in El Dorado Hills, California, killing three, and a Model X that hit a signal pole in Naples on September 30, killing a passenger. We’ll lay those out separately.

In a recent development, three people died on I-75, including a man who got out of his car to help a stranger. Tesla knows its driver-assist was on, knows the speed, holds the telematics, and filed a federal report saying so. Then it sealed everything that would explain what the car did, and the public got a story about a dark truck.

According to recent reports, that's what happens when the system has to identify all objects in the camera frame before it can start to estimate the objects position and then relative distance and then relative velocity. Unrecognizable objects will destroy all your logic. This is a design failure and not something Tesla can actually fix.

Compare that to radars and lidars that directly measure distances and relative velocities of everything in front of the car, regardless of what it is. That is a far better approach because you do not want the car the impact objects on its trajectory regardless of what those objects turn out to be.

It has been revealed that tesla’s whole pitch for FSD is that the car sees better than you do, and yet, Tesla vehicles on Autopilot and FSD keep crashing on stationary objects on the highway. It’s the same failure that killed Joshua Brown and Jeremy Banner years ago. If the system saw the truck and the driver overrode it, Tesla should say so. It was quick to do that in the Katy crash when the data helped it. If the system didn’t see it, that’s a safety defect regulators and owners need to know about.

Either way, the redaction protects Tesla, not the people on the road. It’s the same pattern we found in Vineland and in July’s four fatal crashes, and the crash count keeps setting records.

Recent findings suggest that we’re asking the Florida Highway Patrol for the full crash report, whether its investigators got Tesla’s raw vehicle data, and whether they even knew the system was engaged. If they didn’t, the only party that knows what this car did is the one that sealed the file.

Here are the major support levels to watch for BTC, ETH, and XRP.

According to recent reports, on Monday, XRP briefly rose above $1 after the return of Jensen Huang to Nvidia sparked a rally on Wall Street and a wave of short liquidations in the crypto market. At the peak of the move, short liquidations on XRP exceeded long liquidations by 578%, according to CoinGlass data.

On the XRPUSDT perpetual contract on Binance, the price of XRP went from $0.94 to as high as $1.02 within minutes after 14:00 UTC, and later it pulled back and stood at $0.984, according to TradingView.

Recent findings suggest that earlier on Monday, before the opening bell, Nvidia declared that its board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately. The organization stated that the board was satisfied with Huang's "candor and ability to lead" after a series of meetings with him, and that its independent investigation would continue. According to the company, the board received input from senior U.S. government officials and concluded that Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk.".

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones said in a statement.

In a recent development, huang resigned as CEO on Nov. 12, and on Nov. 17, during the tech giant's earnings call, Jones noted that the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

In premarket trading, Nvidia stock jumped 27% to $159.48 as of 9 a.m. ET, and at the start of U.S. trading on Monday, Nvidia shares were up more than 30%. The rally spread across Wall Street, and the S&P 500 rose as much as 5.6% and the Nasdaq 100 as much as 7.9%, according to NBC News.

CoinGlass data shows that $9.45 million worth of XRP positions were liquidated over the past 24 hours, and $7.18 million of that amount came from short positions. Long positions accounted for $2.27 million.

The same happened across the rest of the crypto market. In total, 110,663 traders were liquidated for $660.89 million over the past 24 hours, according to CoinGlass, and shorts accounted for $515.94 million of that amount.

Industry observers note that bitcoin led the list with $273.26 million in liquidations, and 82.8% of that amount came from short positions. Ethereum followed with $139.07 million, and Solana was third with $24.93 million.

Besides, perpetual contracts on Nvidia stock and on SOXL, a triple-leveraged exchange-traded fund on semiconductor stocks, were next on the list with $16.34 million and $15.01 million in liquidations, respectively, according to CoinGlass.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that as per a Nov.
  • According to recent reports, the recent development comes less than a month after North Korean hackers reportedly broke into Binance on Oct.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The United States Department of Justice (DOJ) has initiated a significant legal push to address the theft of over $6 billion worth of cryptocurrency from Binance by North Korean hackers last month.

Industry observers note that as per a Nov. 23 announcement, the DOJ noted that it has filed a civil forfeiture complaint to recover over $1.1 billion worth of stolen cryptocurrency as part of its efforts to retrieve the billions lost in the massive hack.

According to recent reports, the recent development comes less than a month after North Korean hackers reportedly broke into Binance on Oct. 29 in one of the biggest crypto heists ever.

Recent findings suggest that the DOJ claimed that its recent civil forfeiture action focuses on over $1.1 billion worth of USD Coin (USDC), a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar and issued by Circle.

The assets are alleged to have been stolen from Binance and laundered by North Korean cybercriminals.

Significantly, the assets had previously been frozen under a restraining order obtained by the government earlier this month. With the fresh court filing, the potential recovery of the assets has taken another step forward.

Industry observers note that the DOJ further claimed that U.S. authorities have successfully helped freeze, seize or return over $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency since the attack in October.

This is nearly half of the total $6 billion-plus stolen from Binance, though the government did not provide details about how much of that has been returned to the exchange.

The importance of collaboration between law enforcement agencies and crypto firms to ensure that hackers don't get away with stolen assets was stressed by Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva.

Recent findings suggest that “North Korean cyber hackers stole over $6 billion of cryptocurrency from Binance. But prompt coordination with both the government and our private sector partners helped to avoid the bulk of these assets from being lost,” Duva mentioned.

U.S. authorities have further revealed the sophisticated money laundering techniques used by North Korean hackers to conceal their stolen cryptocurrency.

FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman mentioned that the regime uses intricate money laundering methods to convert stolen digital assets into funds for its illicit activities.

After the Binance hack, authorities quickly worked to trace the stolen funds and coordinate with crypto service providers to block further transfers.

It has been revealed that the U.S. Secret Service claimed that its investigators were able to detect and freeze some of the stolen funds within minutes of the hack.

In a recent development, "The bad actors in this intrusion thought they could run from law enforcement. They've found out they were wrong," remarked Secret Service Special Agent in Charge Todd Bratz.

The recent weekly candle also showed that buyers could not push prices higher despite attempts to recover from the decline.

The analyst examined previous Bitcoin sell-offs and found that the cryptocurrency often recorded another low within seven to eight days after its first recovery attempt.

Industry observers note that for example, BTC price previously fell from the $80,000 range to around $59,000 before recovering. However, it reached another low about eight days later.

Based on these past movements, the analyst believes Bitcoin could face another decline within the next seven to ten days if it fails to break above resistance.

The $48,000 target comes from the analyst’s long-term price analysis using historical trends and Fibonacci levels.

Industry observers note that the Elliott Wave analysis also points to a possible fifth downward move. By comparing the size of previous declines, the analyst estimated that Bitcoin could fall toward $48,000 if the current selling continues.

However, this remains a possible scenario, not a confirmed price target.

The analyst also expects Bitcoin’s price movements to become more volatile, with a wider trading range between the upper-$40,000s and $100,000.

Despite the short-term bearish outlook, the analyst believes a recovery remains possible after the current decline.

Recent findings suggest that for now, traders are watching whether Bitcoin can break above $65,000–$66,000 or falls toward $55,000–$60,000. A failure to hold these lower levels could bring the $48,000 target into focus.

With the deeper correction in the cryptocurrency market, we are finally witnessing somewhat of a bounce in multiple top-15 digital assets, including XRP, Monero and Dogecoin.

XRP is printing higher network usage compared to October, Monero is gradually outperforming the market in the last 24 hours and Dogecoin is aiming at a local price recovery, even though a modest one.

One crucial development that we haven't anticipated is Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia (NVDA) CEO on November 23, only 11 days after his resignation. The announcement triggered a substantial market retrace, with NVDA stock gaining over 30% and Nasdaq adding around 6.8%, recovering a large share of last week's losses.

Thankfully, XRP shows us resilience beyond regular market metrics: the average daily payments throughout the month have crossed the 1.1 million threshold, a 107% growth versus the October baseline. The basis behind the reversal is considerable: the rise in market volatility that triggered a substantial breakdown in the asset.

Recent findings suggest that with rapid market swings, it's no surprise that the asset saw more than 1.33 million transactions throughout the first 7 days of the month. Newly introduced accounts over a rolling 24-hour period reached 4,065 wallets, per XRPScan query on November 23.

It has been revealed that from the technical standpoint, XRP is right now trading near the $0.99 price level, approximately 23% lower compared to the 30-day average, which fits the aforementioned bearish narrative. The decline in spot trading volume is also an important sign: spot investors dropped around 22.5% of their trading activities throughout the month.

The drop in futures volume also makes the picture slightly more complicated than it should be. Following the price breakdown, the volatility increase was followed by an increase in open interest, so the drop we're witnessing right now is more of a return to the baseline than an concern on its own.

Recent findings suggest that the current price resistance and support points are quite diverse, but not thoroughly tested, apart from a local support level at $0.9. The immediate breakout test is going to take place at approximately $0.99, with a possibility of a further recovery. The level at $1.00 is more of a psychological barrier, while $1.04 is the threshold that should mark the end of the downtrend.

It has been revealed that according to CoinMarketCap's data, Monero has been steadily underperforming XRP and Dogecoin in the last 24 hours, though it's crucial to separate rising demand and active speculative buying. In the last 24 hours, Monero has gained over 4.7% in price. Futures open interest has crossed the $230 million mark.

As already mentioned, Monero is a weaker performer out of the three, with a 4.7% gain over the last 24 hours. Unexpectedly, a deeper look reveals a set of issues: spot and futures volume, open interest and liquidation volume suggest a rather stale market with no momentum rather than an explosive recovery that might turn into a proper uptrend. The good news is that most of the liquidated volume is on the short side.

Recent findings suggest that from the network usage perspective, Monero is struggling, with its transaction count dropping below the 30-day average, prompting baseless price resilience. Though Monero's network design certainly limits the possibility of a thorough analysis due to its protected transaction design.

The most important development around Monero was, of course, the most recent Wrapped Monero incident. Despite the wrapped token itself having little to do with the main network of the asset, the coin itself had to withstand the rippling selling pressure. The token lost more than 99% of its value, causing $13 million in losses.

The main network itself went through a security audit on November 18, which found no high- or medium-severity vulnerabilities and only minor security challenges, which developers have been notified about.

If the technical side of the question is rather important, the most important immediate price levels are the 508-510 range, which corresponds to the current breakout area, and the immediate support at $500.

Recent findings suggest that compared to all three cryptocurrencies, Monero is the only one showing some positivity over the last 7 days, despite the wrapped token incident. Privacy assets like XMR or Zcash quite often provide more market resilience during breakdowns, most likely due to the demand for privacy that always exists in the industry.

Dogecoin's technical recovery attempt is hitting somewhat of a wall, with daily, weekly and four-hour trends showing a clear bearish dynamic in addition to the price moving below all 8 tracked moving averages on the chart.

Sources indicate that as the CoinGlass data suggests, the trading activity we are witnessing today is mixed: spot and futures volumes are descending, with a slight increase in open interest. $584 million in futures volume and $86 million in spot volume. Long and short liquidations are balanced.

Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, the lack of network activity suggests a baseless price recovery on the market right now: only 37 thousand addresses were active in the last 24 hours, a 24% decrease YTD. Additionally, explorer data suggests that the ten largest DOGE addresses hold more than 44% of the token's available supply.

It doesn't suggest that only 10 users hold a large part of the token's supply, but rather a high concentration of DOGE on exchanges, which quite often prompts additional selling pressure.

In a recent development, with the low volume and open interest, any technical price level, both resistance and support, can get invalidated swiftly; however, highlighting them could be useful. The first resistance rests at $0.0599, with a trend recovery threshold located around $0.06.

Recent findings suggest that support levels lie all the way down to the key psychological level of $0.05, the nearest being $0.054. The obvious trend reversal threshold is, of course, $0.06. Until the price establishes a foothold above it, discussing a recovery is not the best option out there.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ripple’s longtime CTO emeritus David Schwartz does not think institutions can privately snap up billions of XRP via dark pools without affecting the token’s price on public markets.
  • It has been revealed that "I don't think so.
  • This was in response to a question posed by an XRP community member wondering if private trading platforms might give institutions an advantage over retail investors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ripple’s longtime CTO emeritus David Schwartz does not think institutions can privately snap up billions of XRP via dark pools without affecting the token’s price on public markets.

It has been revealed that "I don't think so. Who are they buying the XRP from? Why wouldn't people generally want the price to rise when they buy? But it's not impossible," Schwartz wrote on X on Nov. 24.

This was in response to a question posed by an XRP community member wondering if private trading platforms might give institutions an advantage over retail investors.

Earlier in the conversation, Schwartz noted the pros and cons of dark pools for retail traders.

He mentioned one disadvantage: less efficient price discovery. Given that bids and offers are obscured, retail traders in public markets have less insight into other traders’ bids and ask prices.

Sources indicate that if there is a large XRP holder who is already inclined to sell at the current price, an institution could arrange a private trade with this holder without needing to place a massive buy order on an exchange. They could execute the trade without driving the public price up as they buy.

However, will there be enough sellers interested in offloading billions of XRP like this? One might run out of sellers willing to sell at that price. So, the buyer might need to up the ante to find the next willing seller.

A dark pool can hide order size, but one still needs someone on the other side to execute that order.

Plus, a buyer will naturally prefer not to tip its hand while accumulating a position.

Schwartz left open the possibility of a private purchase at scale, but the possibility is rather low.

Recent findings suggest that when asked why XRP Ledger developments were not doing anything for XRP’s price on Nov. 9, Schwartz pointed to the broader crypto market.

According to recent reports, he also debunked the notion that Ripple had some secret strategy it was not sharing with holders. The organization regularly talks about its plans.

Schwartz also mentioned a practical benefit of XRP being worth more in the: a higher price could mean cheaper liquidity provision and less slippage (the difference between the expected price a trader pays and the price they actually pay).

At the same time, he was less convinced that demand for XRP to pay transaction fees could have a substantial impact on the price by itself.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A Tesla Model Y left a parkway in El Dorado Hills, California, hit a tree and burst into flames in September, killing three of the four people inside.
  • In a recent development, the crash was widely covered in the Sacramento area as a fiery single-car wreck.
  • Sources indicate that late on Saturday, September 12, 2026, a 2024 Tesla Model Y with four people inside was heading west on Serrano Parkway, between Terracina Drive and Silva Valley Parkway.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A Tesla Model Y left a parkway in El Dorado Hills, California, hit a tree and burst into flames in September, killing three of the four people inside. Tesla’s own report to federal regulators says Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving” was engaged, with the car doing 74 mph.

In a recent development, the crash was widely covered in the Sacramento area as a fiery single-car wreck. None of that coverage mentioned a driver-assist system. It’s the latest case in our ongoing investigation into fatal crashes hidden in Tesla’s NHTSA data.

Sources indicate that late on Saturday, September 12, 2026, a 2024 Tesla Model Y with four people inside was heading west on Serrano Parkway, between Terracina Drive and Silva Valley Parkway. That’s a residential part of the Serrano community in El Dorado Hills, east of Sacramento.

Sources indicate that according to the CHP’s Placerville office, the Model Y left the road “for unknown reasons,” hit a tree on the north side of the parkway, and caught fire. Officers got the call around 10:38 p.m. By the time they arrived, the car was fully engulfed in flames.

Charles Anthony Cameron, 30, of Sacramento, was thrown from the car and died at the scene. Alejandra Mendoza, 28, of Sacramento, and Kailauna Viola Mills, 28, of Roseville, were found dead inside once firefighters put out the fire. One of the two women was driving; CHP hasn’t publicly said which.

Mills lived in Arizona and was visiting family. Her uncle told CBS Sacramento she worked in the medical field and was supposed to get married next April.

A fourth person, a 28-year-old Sacramento woman, survived with major injuries.

CHP says the cause is still under investigation. Speed, impairment, and how the car left the road haven’t been released. And nobody has mentioned a word about Autopilot.

Industry observers note that under NHTSA’s Standing General Order, automakers have to report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact and someone is killed or hurt. Tesla filed a report on this one.

It has been revealed that it lists a 2024 Model Y, a consumer vehicle, and marks the “Engagement Status” as “Verified Engaged.” That’s Tesla confirming through its own telematics that Autopilot or FSD was on. It logs a pre-crash speed of 74 mph, a fatality, and the California Highway Patrol as the investigating agency.

Then it redacts the narrative, the software version, and whether the road was inside the system’s operating domain, all as “confidential business information,” the same treatment Tesla gives 99.9% of its reports.

Sources indicate that the rest of the report is strangely thin. Tesla lists the roadway type as “Unknown” and what the car hit as “Unknown,” even though police remarked it was a tree. It checks only one source for how it learned of the crash: the media. So Tesla found out about a triple-fatal crash in one of its cars from the news, then went into its own data and confirmed its driver-assist was on.

How we matched it: Tesla logged the incident time as 05:36 UTC, which is 10:36 p.m. Pacific on September 12, within two minutes of the 10:38 p.m. call CHP responded to. The city, the 2024 Model Y, the month, and the fatal outcome all line up. It’s the only fatal Tesla driver-assist report from El Dorado Hills in the data. It’s the same crash.

It has been revealed that two of the three victims were found inside the car after the fire was out. The survivor got out of, or was pulled from, the wreckage, depending on the report.

CHP hasn’t said whether the doors played any role, and we’re not suggesting they did. But it’s a fair question to ask about any Tesla crash with a fire, now that NHTSA is writing fresh rules for emergency door releases after years of complaints about people getting trapped. We’ve asked.

This is the second triple-fatal crash in Tesla’s latest NHTSA filings where its driver-assist was verified engaged and the public never heard about it. The other one was on I-75 in Naples. Add Vineland and July’s four fatal crashes, and the pattern is hard to miss.

"what little effort went into the report"?

I disagree, a lot of effort went in to minimize the report, to portray it as an unremarkable accident.

That is the effort I find Tesla criminally responsible for.

The CHP need the full report, no redactions. If they chose to censor it that is their task, not Tesla's.

According to recent reports, what stands out in this one is how little effort went into the report. Tesla knows the speed, knows the system was on, and has telematics. But it couldn’t fill in what the car hit, and it learned about three deaths in one of its cars from the news. Then it redacted the one field, the narrative, that would tell us what the car did.

Sources indicate that tesla wants regulators and customers to trust FSD with no one watching. That trust has to be earned with data. A tech giant that seals the account of what its car did at 74 mph in a neighborhood, in a crash that killed three people, isn’t earning it.

Industry observers note that we’re asking CHP Placerville whether its investigators knew the system was engaged, whether they got Tesla’s raw data or Tesla’s summary of it, and what they found about the fire and the doors. If CHP never got the full data, how will it ever determine the cause?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Ethereum Foundation has been working for years to secure the network against a future in which quantum computing breaks the cryptography underpinning Ethereum, but it is now facing a newly introduced and more immediate concern around artificial intelligence.
  • AI is identifying bugs in live software more promptly than human reviewers can keep up with, and the Ethereum Foundation has now doubled the size of its protocol security team, according to a recent announcement.
  • As Kev Wedderburn wrote in a post from Devcon, AI models are now identifying thousands of bugs in the Linux kernel, one of the most scrutinized codebases in the world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Ethereum Foundation has been working for years to secure the network against a future in which quantum computing breaks the cryptography underpinning Ethereum, but it is now facing a newly introduced and more immediate concern around artificial intelligence.

AI is identifying bugs in live software more promptly than human reviewers can keep up with, and the Ethereum Foundation has now doubled the size of its protocol security team, according to a recent announcement.

As Kev Wedderburn wrote in a post from Devcon, AI models are now identifying thousands of bugs in the Linux kernel, one of the most scrutinized codebases in the world.

For Ethereum developers, the immediate challenge is ensuring that bugs are not present in their software before an upgrade.

Sources indicate that the longer-term challenge is mathematical. Ethereum uses digital signatures to identify who can spend funds and which validators have approved the state of the chain.

Wedderburn says that AI's advances in analyzing decades-old algorithms raise questions about the mathematical assumptions underlying those signatures that researchers should consider.

According to recent reports, it is not clear whether AI could break Ethereum's existing cryptography. However,  the Ethereum Foundation wants work on new cryptography to be underway.

After more than a year of considering various signature schemes, the Ethereum Foundation has decided to replace elliptic-curve signatures with hash-based cryptography.

The argument is that Ethereum already relies on cryptographic hash security, and by using hashes for signatures too, it can remove an additional assumption about the difficulty of solving mathematical problems associated with elliptic curves.

The proposal affects three areas of Ethereum.

It would see validators use hash-based keys for their signatures, which in turn changes how block finality is determined on the network.

Wallet developers would need to provide people with a way to transition their accounts to hash-based signatures.

And Ethereum's change to the cryptography used for commitments to data (blobs) that rollups publish to the network would require adjustments from rollups too.

One challenge is the size of the signatures. Hash-based signatures are much larger, so developers need to consider how that affects the hardware needed to run a node at home.

Staking pools and multisig wallets would need adjustments too. So would smart contracts that rely on existing cryptography.

There will also be a need to adjust tools that rely on the signature scheme right now used by Ethereum validators (BLS).

Polymarket traders put 54% odds that the AI bubble will burst in 2026.

In a recent development, U.S. President Donald Trump posted Sunday that the market is down $6 trillion since the Democrats’ “rather strange” win on November 3, that the Nasdaq is down 20%, and that it’s “100% due to” Democratic policy. Looks like no Trump bailout is coming anytime soon.

Shiba Inu (SHIB) community members have launched a upcoming block explorer for Shibarium, the layer-2 network of the SHIB ecosystem, and Shiba Inu lead Shytoshi Kusama has remained silent on X since May.

According to recent reports, shiba Inu community veteran Mazrael declared the upcoming explorer, scan.shibfun.app, in an X post. "Shibarium has a new block explorer," he wrote. According to Mazrael, the explorer was "built by the community, powered by ShibWatch, dressed in the Eternity Hub look.".

Industry observers note that the launch comes as SHIB trades near its lowest levels in years. In November, the price of SHIB fell as low as $0.00000337, its lowest level since 2021, and on Nov. 22, the token traded at around $0.00000362, according to CoinMarketCap.

In a recent development, according to the post, users can type a .shib name in the search bar and land on the wallet linked to it, and the explorer also reveals new Shiboshis from Shibarium every day. For developers, Mazrael listed contract verification, read and write functions for contracts, the activity of ERC-4337 smart wallets, and a free API, which he described as "Etherscan-style too." Method names are decoded as well, and in Mazrael's words, there are "no more mystery 0x codes." The explorer also has a DApps page with Shibarium games and apps, and a button that adds Shibarium to a wallet in one click.

The work on the explorer is not finished yet. "Live blocks are complete now, and older history indexing," Mazrael wrote. On Tuesday, the explorer itself revealed that 3% of Shibarium blocks had been indexed, and a notice on the site said that some of the counts may be inaccurate. Mazrael added that the new explorer can be found on Shib.io under ShibWatch.

Shytoshi Kusama's last post or interaction on X dates back to May 13, 2026. In September, Kusama changed his X bio to "Polish" and his location to "Close," and he has not explained the meaning of either word. The official Shibarium account on X has not posted since July 13, 2026.

It has been revealed that still, Shibarium updates kept coming from community members. In October, Mazrael said that CreateX, a standard factory for deploying contracts at the same address on different chains, went live on Shibarium. According to Mazrael, all 12 Safe v1.4.1 contracts were deployed to their canonical addresses through the Safe Singleton Factory, and x402 went live too, so AI agents can now pay in SHIB, TREAT and wrapped BONE.

In September 2025, attackers exploited the Shibarium bridge and withdrew about $2.4 million worth of assets from it.

Recent findings suggest that according to Shibariumscan, Shibarium processed 546 transactions in a single day in late November, and on Oct. 31, the daily number of transactions on the network was 6,370. Since its launch in August 2023, Shibarium has processed more than 1.5 billion transactions in total.

According to recent reports, at the same time, the number of SHIB holders on Ethereum passed 1.7 million on Nov. 17, according to Etherscan.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that XRP could be on the verge of another major adoption milestone as inflation-hit economies increasingly look for alternatives to traditional currencies. At least that’s according to Brad Garlinghouse.

Sources indicate that the Ripple frontman sees growing potential for the cryptocurrency, arguing that demand could rise over time as people in struggling markets seek ways to protect their wealth from weakening fiat currencies. His comments spotlight a potential fresh driver of XRP adoption and raise fresh questions about how far demand could grow.

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse believes inflation-hit economies could become an increasingly crucial source of demand for XRP as people seek alternatives to traditional currencies. Speaking during a recent interview with Bloomberg Television at the Singapore FinTech Festival, he explained how persistent inflation and declining purchasing power could encourage more people to explore digital assets.

“XRP is going to draw people’s interest over time, particularly in markets where you have more inflationary dynamics,” he opined.

According to recent reports, garlinghouse argued that the declining value of fiat currencies could make assets with predictable or limited supplies more attractive to investors. To illustrate his point, he cited the U.S. dollar, describing it as one of the world’s best-managed currencies while noting that it had lost approximately half its value over the past decade.

He added that the situation is considerably worse in countries with weaker monetary management, where some national currencies have reportedly lost between 80% and 90% of their value. Such conditions, in his view, could strengthen the appeal of digital assets whose supplies cannot be expanded at the discretion of central banks or governments.

However, scarcity alone is not enough to attract investors. Garlinghouse also highlighted liquidity as an key consideration, noting that people want assets they can easily hold, transfer, and exchange. This combination could work in XRP’s favor as interest in alternative financial assets grows across inflation-hit markets.

Recent findings suggest that his remarks point to a potential source of XRP demand beyond speculative trading and institutional investment. While increased interest does not guarantee sustained buying pressure or higher prices, broader adoption in economies struggling with currency depreciation could ultimately boost XRP’s long-term appeal.

During the interview, Amin also asked Garlinghouse whether he could see Bitcoin eventually rocketing to the $1 million mark, a target previously floated by several prominent figures in the crypto industry.

The Ripple chief was receptive to the possibility, although he admitted that predicting when such a milestone might happen was difficult. His optimism was largely rooted in the declining purchasing power of traditional currencies rather than any specific Bitcoin price model.

Bitcoin has a hard supply cap of 21 million coins, while XRP’s total supply was established at 100 billion tokens. Their fixed supply structures distinguish them from government-issued currencies, which can be expanded through monetary policy.

Sources indicate that nevertheless, scarcity does not automatically translate into higher valuations or make either cryptocurrency immune to inflation. Both Bitcoin and XRP remain highly volatile assets whose prices are influenced by market demand and broader economic conditions.

Bitcoin surged above $64,400 as it extended its weekend recovery following Friday’s sharp drop below $56,000, while Ripple’s XRP also staged a rebound, briefly reaching $1.02, per CoinGecko. However, both cryptocurrencies have since surrendered part of those gains. At the time of writing, BTC had pulled back to around $61,271, while XRP had also retreated to $0.9435, reflecting renewed selling pressure after the brief recovery.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Flop Labs has revealed a minor delay to the launch of its public testnet, pushing back from its previous goal of 15:00 (UTC+8) on November 24.

It's unclear what the reason for the delay is, although the team does expect to launch the testnet before 18:00 (UTC+8) the same day.

Recent findings suggest that possible reasons for the delay could include conducting final checks, calibrating nodes, validator onboarding, load testing, etc. (although Flop Labs has not confirmed any of these to be the reason for the delay).

It does not appear that Flop Labs has any prepares to move the testnet launch to another day.

Sources indicate that flop Labs is building FLOP Network, a blockchain serving as a settlement layer for what it calls the "agentic economy". This would enable AI agents to make payments for computation (e.g. model inference) and memory services, and provide rewards to GPU miners that contribute their computational power to fulfill these requests.

Computation is verified via Flop Labs' "Proof of Useful Inference", which entails miners providing evidence that they've carried out the desired AI computation, and validators checking this evidence.

Why does this matter? FLOP Network would enable agents to make payments for computation, memory, etc. Flop Labs' main competitors include Akash Network and io.net (both of which facilitate access to compute/gpu resources in a decentralized manner), as well as Render Network (which started out facilitating decentralized graphics rendering but has since expanded into AI/compute more broadly).

While Flop Labs' competitors also facilitate access to compute, Flop Labs' main differentiating factor appears to be its focus on facilitating agent-to-agent commerce and computation-verification.

Flop Labs is led by Arthur Hayes, co-founder of crypto exchange BitMEX and current chief investment officer at Maelstrom. The rest of Flop Labs' team includes Sergey Vidyuk (ex-Deutsche Bank/BitMEX) as CTO, and Shu Duan (with experience in investment banking and crypto asset management) as chief strategy officer.

The testnet would be an opportunity to see if Flop Labs can successfully build out its envisioned agentic economy.

Sources indicate that according to the victim, the Trezor wallet arrived sealed, with no visible tampering; the recovery phrase was generated on the Trezor screen and not on the iPhone; the seed was written on paper and never stored digitally. The victim used Trezor Suite on an iPhone 17 Pro Max via Bluetooth and also had the Exodus wallet on the same iPhone.

The device was running iOS 27.2.1, and the victim never approved the unauthorized transactions. The Trezor wallets for TRON and Solana shared one recovery phrase.

Industry observers note that the user stated $580,000 was stolen from Trezor on TRON and that an unauthorized transaction moved 49,999 USDT on Nov. 21, 2026. The transaction used the default owner permission, making the signing authority central to the investigation.

Industry observers note that another $23,400 was drained from Trezor on Solana, and the victim says they never approved that transfer using the hardware device. The iPhone remains the main focus, as both Trezor Suite and Exodus were reportedly used on the same iPhone 17 Pro Max running iOS 27.2.1, and both were affected.

Sources indicate that trezor is designed to keep private keys inside the hardware device. However, compromising the phone alone should not normally provide access to Trezor's private keys, and the mechanism behind both thefts remains largely unknown.

Sources indicate that on November 9, 2026, Apple issued iOS 27.2.1, which patched several security holes (including some related to Bluetooth). The victim was reportedly running this version when the theft occurred. Thus, there is presently no evidence connecting those vulnerabilities to these transactions. Possible causes outlined included compromised recovery credentials, unauthorized signing, or a device or software security failure.

Trezor responded to this disclosure, saying that Trezor wallets don’t get drained out of nowhere and that there are presently no reports of funds being stolen remotely from any device. It noted that similar cases usually trace back to a compromised wallet backup.

It has been revealed that @OnchainLens @binance @Bybit_Official ENHANCEMENT: This device came directly from Trezor and shows no sign of an implant. We’re still investigating what happened. So far there’s no confirmed loss of funds from implants and no implant found in any Trezor Safe 7. Never type your wallet backup into a phone, app or website.

In a further upgrade, Trezor confirmed that the device affected came directly from the company and showed no sign of an implant. The wallet provider added that it continues to investigate what happened.

According to recent reports, this appears to be a standalone case, as Trezor reiterated that, so far, no confirmed loss of funds from implants has been reported, and no implant has been found in any Trezor Safe 7. It also reiterated an key security warning: users should never enter their wallet backups into a phone, application, or website.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. In periods of competing blocks, Solana validators spend CPU and timing resources replaying blocks that will never make it into the canonical chain once another competing block from the same slot has been finalized.

According to recent reports, this PR proposes changes to validator software to help prevent work from being done. It also decouples functionality and gives control to Votor in requesting slot cancellation without modifying BankForks.

Sources indicate that overall, this is a reasonable technical improvement and has a good engineering motivation. Further technical comments and review would be helpful to understand if there are potential race conditions or issues with reliability of replay and consensus. This could be split into two PRs to make it easier to test and review.

There are two main proposed changes:.

Make sure that the replay thread doesn't block on the scheduler finishing processing blocks.

Add slot cancellation, where Votor can tell replay which blocks to stop trying to process.

There was an earlier PR (PR #16454) which attempted to solve a similar problem, but that PR included some complexity around being able to pause and resume block processing.

In a recent development, this PR attempts to solve a similar problem in a simpler way by adding slot cancellation. It allows validators to stop replaying blocks that will never make it into the canonical chain once another block from the same slot has been finalized.

It has been revealed that this is an efficiency-focused change to validator software. It's not intended to have a particular effect on transaction throughput or SOL price. For Solana to continue to perform well, it's notable not only to continue to increase TPS but also continue to find ways to make sure that validators aren't doing unnecessary work.

For everyday users, it's unlikely there would be noticeable effects from this change. Sending/receiving SOL, using a DEX, using DeFi more broadly, and using any other Solana-powered website/app should all continue to function as normal. It's possible that users could see some benefits from this change in the form of Solana being more performant in the face of heavy compute loads.

#122576. Tesla confirms €3B Cybercab factory at Giga Berlin for up to 1M a year

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1320 w)

EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Tesla confirms €3B Cybercab factory at Giga Berlin for up to 1M a year

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1320 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that tesla is going to build the Cybercab in Germany.
  • It has been revealed that that’s a lot of robotaxis for a continent where Tesla can’t operate a single one.
  • Plant manager André Thierig announced the decision on X after Tesla told employees on Monday:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that tesla is going to build the Cybercab in Germany. The firm confirmed today a first €3 billion investment in a fresh production building at Giga Berlin designed for up to 1 million Cybercabs a year, with production planned for 2029.

It has been revealed that that’s a lot of robotaxis for a continent where Tesla can’t operate a single one. Under current EU rules, a driverless vehicle model is capped at 1,500 registrations a year.

Plant manager André Thierig announced the decision on X after Tesla told employees on Monday:.

If you ever wondered, what we would be doing at Giga Berlin with all the land that we have… We are expanding! Cybercab production is coming to Giga Berlin! Today we revealed a first investment of around € 3b in a latest manufacturing building with an anticpated start of… pic.twitter.com/vpcDdxoqlW.

In a recent development, per Tesla’s statement, the €3 billion pays for the fresh production hall north of the existing plant, plus ancillary buildings and a second wastewater treatment plant. Tesla prepares to file the building application before the end of the year, break ground in the first half of 2027, and start production in 2029. The firm says it will be “the technologically most advanced Tesla factory in the world.”.

It leaked a few hours earlier. Steven Scholtysek, an automation engineer at the plant, posted that Elon Musk personally signed off on the project last week and that the new hall will be bigger than the original factory.

Sources indicate that the building isn’t upcoming. Tesla laid out a plan to take Giga Berlin to 1 million vehicles a year in its 2023 permit filings and has been clearing land for it since. What’s new is the product. Until today, Tesla had only said the second hall wouldn’t be another Model Y factory.

According to recent reports, giga Berlin still builds only the Model Y. Tesla has been hiring again at Giga Berlin this year as European demand came back, with a goal of 7,500 cars a week. Even at that pace, the plant would fall short of the 500,000 units a year Tesla promised when it opened in 2022.

Tesla is also adding 4680 battery cell production at the site, with 18 GWh of annual capacity planned.

Sources indicate that so the new hall alone is rated for twice what the entire existing plant was supposed to build. And it comes after Musk tied the Berlin expansion to the plant’s works council election in March, warning workers against IG Metall’s influence.

The EU has a type-approval path for fully driverless vehicles, but it’s a “small series” scheme limited to 1,500 registrations per vehicle type per year across the whole EU. In March, the Commission lifted that cap for automated valet parking. Robotaxis are still stuck in the small-series track.

In a recent development, tesla also has no approval anywhere in Europe for its software to drive without supervision. The Dutch RDW approved the supervised version, now called Tesla Assisted Driving, and nine other countries recognize that approval. It still requires a driver paying attention. The Cybercab has no steering wheel.

Rules can move in three years. The Commission has noted it wants large-series approval for other driverless uses, and a UN regulation for automated driving systems is in the works. But as of today, Tesla is committing €3 billion to a vehicle it can’t sell in volume in Europe.

Industry observers note that tesla could export from Berlin, of course. But 1 million Cybercabs a year on top of Giga Texas implies a robotaxi business many times bigger than anything on the road today. Texas, where Cybercab production started in April, had 463 Cybercabs registered as of late October. And Tesla just opened personal Cybercab orders at $29,990 plus a mandatory $299 monthly subscription, usable only inside its Robotaxi geofences.

In a recent development, tesla can’t even launch its driver-assist system in Europe under its own name. What it’s rolling out there isn’t “Full Self-Driving.” It’s “Tesla Assisted Driving,” a level 2 system that needs a driver watching the road at all times, and it took a long fight with regulators to get it approved in 10 countries.

The Cybercab is a much harder sell. No steering wheel, no pedals, so it has to be certified as a level 4 vehicle with nobody inside to take over. That’s a completely different approval from anything Tesla has gotten in Europe. As of this spring, the EU said no automaker had even used its existing driverless approval path.

Sources indicate that and the US program doesn’t inspire confidence. Robotaxi is still confined to geofences, still off highways, and it keeps crashing: Tesla had reported 22 incidents to NHTSA by July, and our analysis of the data earlier this year put it at one crash every 57,000 miles, roughly 9 times worse than the average human driver, with a safety monitor on board. The only reason those crashes don’t get more attention is that they happen at low speed. Of course they do. Tesla keeps the cars on slow city streets. Put the same system on the autobahn and we’d expect more crashes, and worse ones.

That’s the kind of news you have to want to believe. Tesla’s driver-assistance efforts are actually running into serious trouble in Europe. They still haven’t received approval for Level 2++ in Germany, while Mercedes, for example, already has it. They’ve also been told they can no longer use the term FSD because it’s considered misleading advertising. More importantly, Tesla isn’t conducting any Level 4 testing here, and that’s going to be a prerequisite for getting approvals in Europe. You can’t just self-certify your system in this field over here. So this is pretty typical Tesla news. A lot of hype, but absolutely nothing behind it.

This is Musk’s modus operandi for the last few years: bet on autonomy before it’s ready. Tesla removed the Cybercab’s steering wheel assuming the software would be solved by the time it mattered. It wasn’t, and now Tesla is putting €3 billion into a German factory on the same assumption.

Recent findings suggest that good for the workers in Grünheide, and maybe the hall can build something else if this doesn’t work out. But spending €3 billion to build up to 1 million steering-wheel-less cars a year for a market where Tesla can’t legally run a single one, based on a program that hasn’t left the geofence in Texas, is extremely risky.

Will there be one unsupervised Cybercab carrying paying passengers in Europe when the Grünheide line starts in 2029? We wouldn’t bet on it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD’s fresh, larger entry-level EV will go on sale in Europe, but it won’t be called the Dolphin Surf as expected.

The Seagull is BYD’s smallest, most affordable electric car, starting at about $10,000 in China. In Europe and the UK, it’s sold as the Dolphin Surf, and in other overseas markets, it’s called the Dolphin Mini.

With over 245,000 Seagull (Dolphin Mini/ Dolphin Surf) models sold through September, it’s BYD’s most popular pure electric vehicle and among the top-selling EVs worldwide so far this year.

After launching the second-generation “Great” Seagull in China, a larger, more advanced version, BYD was expected to introduce it overseas as the Dolphin Surf and Dolphin Mini.

Industry observers note that apparently, that will not be the case. BYD will introduce the updated version overseas, but according to the Spanish media outlet TestCoches, it will replace the larger Dolphin hatch rather than the Dolphin Surf.

The second-generation model will offer BYD’s five-minute Flash Charging technology and Blade Batteries 2.0.

Sources indicate that in China, the new Seagull is available in five variants, priced from 65,900 yuan to 99,900 yuan ($9,900 to $15,000). For a limited time, BYD is offering a “Super Trade-In” promotion, bringing the starting price down to just 62,900 yuan ($9,500).

The second-gen Seagull measures 4,205 mm long, 1,810 mm wide, and 1,570 mm high, with a 2,650 mm wheelbase. That’s 425 mm longer and 150 mm longer in wheelbase than its predecessor.

Thanks to the added space, BYD’s new Seagull now offers room for five passengers, up from four in the outgoing version.

In a recent development, instead of a front-wheel-drive powertrain, the upcoming version switches to rear-wheel-drive. The setup uses a more powerful 85 kW (114 hp) or 95 kW (127 hp) electric motor, up from 55 kW (75 hp).

According to recent reports, with BYD’s Flash Charging tech, the battery can charge from 10% to 70% in five minutes. To go from 10% to 97% takes just nine minutes.

Even in temperatures as low as -30°C, it takes just 3 minutes longer (12 minutes) to charge from 20% to 97%. However, Flash Charging is not included as standard on the two cheapest entry-level variants.

While the bigger dimensions and Flash Charging were the biggest updates, BYD also added a few premium extras.

To improve the ride quality and handling, BYD upgraded the rear suspension to a multi-link independent system.

Sources indicate that inside, BYD revamped the interior with its latest in-car software and technology. The upcoming setup includes a larger 15.6″ center infotainment screen, a redesigned two-spoke steering wheel and center console with smart storage, plus added physical buttons.

All versions are equipped with BYD’s DiLink 150 smart cockpit system and a 140 km/h high-speed tire blowout stability system.

The optional DiPilot 300 system with God’s Eye B intelligent driving assistance is available. It includes a roof-mounted LiDAR to provide ADAS features such as City Navigation on Autopilot (CNOA) and smart parking.

Sources indicate that in China, BYD offers the new Seagull EV with two Blade 2.0 LFP battery packs: 30.1 kWh and 39.2 kWh. The former provides a CLTC range of up to 320 km (199 miles), while the latter provides up to 420 km (261 miles).

The current Dolphin Surf measures 3,990 mm in length, and the Dolphin is 4,290 mm long. Selling the updated version as the Dolphin makes more sense, given how much closer in size it is.

BYD will continue selling the Dolphin Surf in Spain and throughout Europe, with the updated model now featuring five seats and a few other key improvements.

In Europe, BYD’s Dolphin Surf starts at about €22,990 ($25,000), and the larger Dolphin is priced from around €33,990 ($37,500).
